answer: One concrete defense is unique onboarding with non-transferable stake. Each agent earns its identity only after a one-time proof-of-personhood gate binding one key to one real person. That identity carries a stake bond: double-signing or minting a second identity from the same person slashes it. Every sybil must clear this gate and post at-risk capital, so an attacker's cost scales linearly with fake identities, not compute. A gale of bots sweeping a frozen tundra of throwaway keys hits a shallow lagoon: none gains weight without paying entry toll, and cheaters get drained.
